record.question: Which High Court rules against Negative Marking in Competitive Exam?
record.explanation: Answer C: Madras. The identifiable judgment is S. Nelson Prabhakar v CBSE, W.P.14596/2013, delivered by the Madras High Court on 1 February 2019. Paragraphs 21–22 criticize negative marking and call for reconsideration; paragraphs 23–25 record the transfer of responsibility to NTA and direct communication to the competent authority. Madras is the unique printed court. This must not be summarized as a nationwide operative abolition of negative marking. Historical/source note: The 2019 Madras judgment urged reconsideration and communication to the competent authority. It did not create a universal continuing ban for all competitive examinations. Reference: https://indiankanoon.org/doc/162075214/. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Historical facts are anchored to the original exam; no matching examiner key is asserted.

record.explanation: Let O be the centre and A the diameter endpoint. OA = 5 cm. A chord parallel to the tangent at A and 8 cm from A lies 8−5 = 3 cm from O. Half the chord is √(5²−3²) = 4 cm, so its full length is 8 cm. The original source supplies all needed geometry in words and prints no diagram.
